terms.gloss: a siege engine for hurling stones
terms.comment: Lewis & Short prefer ballista to balista. Strictly the stone-thrower, as against the catapulta, which shot arrows; later the names were used for each other (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a siege engine for shooting arrows and stones

phrases.latin: meus est ballista pugnus, cubitus catapulta est mihi, umerus ariēs
phrases.english: my fist is a ballista, my elbow is a catapult, my shoulder a battering ram

phrases.latin: Heus, tū mihi nōn bracchium, sed ballistam habēre vidēris, ita torquēs globum.
phrases.english: Hey, it isn’t an arm you’ve got, it’s a catapult, the way you hurl the ball!
phrases.source: Erasm. Coll., Lūsus puerīlēs, Globī, I 41

sources: Lewis & Short: ballista · Lewis & Short: catapulta
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-erasmus), checked against the editions named there.
